_what: The ORDER backlog work is taken in. Membership is a `family: <slug>` label; ORDER is a `blocks: <slug>` label; this file declares that a dependency EXISTS, which is what makes an empty query mean 'unblocked' rather than 'nobody ever labelled a blocker'.
_criterion: Order by EVIDENCE DEPENDENCY, not severity: work whose fix needs another oracle to be accepted sorts after that oracle is reachable.
_why_not_keyed_to_a_family: It was, for one day, and a live query falsified it the same afternoon. The family `oracle-cannot-reach` is the general class -- an oracle that cannot reach what it certifies -- and #2224 joined it: a GPU performance benchmark that dies before it times anything. Its mechanism is the family's exactly, and it blocks nothing about convergence, because what it certifies is speed. A family is the unit of GROUPING and a dependency is a relation of ORDER, and the two do not share a grain: keyed to the family, one unrelated member holds the queue head shut forever. So the blocker carries its own label, applied to the issues that actually stand in the way.

dependencies.why: MMS is this library's only external oracle for correctness; 'does this scheme converge' has no trustworthy test until it reaches most solvers. The five issues that carried this closed between 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-13; the last, #1991, closed on 2026-09-13 and nothing noticed for eight days, which is why the trigger exists.
